title: Microsoft Marketplace Request Private Offer
summary: Microsoft's Request Private Offer lets buyers ask for a private offer from your listing. How to enable it, route the lead, and qualify the deal fast.
body_markdown:
*Microsoft’s Request Private Offer is a listing-page control that lets a prospective buyer ask a seller for custom pricing or terms directly from an Azure Marketplace listing — turning a listing that only generated awareness into one that captures negotiated-deal demand.*


---


A Microsoft commercial marketplace listing has always been good at being found and bad at being asked. A buyer could read the page, start a free trial, even subscribe to a public plan — but if what they actually wanted was a negotiated price on a three-year term, the listing gave them nowhere to say so. They left the page and emailed someone, or they didn’t.


Request Private Offer closes that gap. The buyer raises their hand from the listing itself, and the deal starts as an inbound lead instead of a cold outbound guess. Which means the hard part is no longer generating the interest — it’s answering it fast enough to matter.


---


## **What is Microsoft’s Request Private Offer?**


Request Private Offer is a setting a publisher turns on during offer setup that lets a customer request customized pricing or terms directly from the offer’s Marketplace listing page. Microsoft made it available on July 20, 2026. Alongside the request, the buyer can share details about their intended use case, so the seller has context before the first reply.


It is the missing inbound half of the private-offer motion. Sellers could already *send* an[Azure Marketplace private offer](https://www.suger.io/resources/blog/azure-private-offers-vs-private-plans/) ; now a buyer can *ask* for one without leaving the listing. The listing stops being a dead end for high-intent traffic.


---


## **How a request reaches your team**


A submitted request does not sit in a Marketplace inbox nobody watches. It flows through the same lead-management path the commercial marketplace already uses: Marketplace referrals, supported APIs, and connected CRM integrations. Each request is captured as a marketplace lead in the referrals workspace, where your sales team engages it and builds the tailored private offer.


That routing is the whole point, and it is also the whole risk. A request is a warm lead with a clock on it. If it lands in a workspace no one owns, the feature has simply moved the place where deals go quiet — from “the buyer never asked” to “we never answered.” The plumbing that carries the lead into the system your team actually works in is what decides whether Request Private Offer earns anything.


---


## **Which offers can use it**


Request Private Offer is available for eligible transactable offers across the main commercial-marketplace types: SaaS offers, Azure application offers, Azure container offers, and Azure Virtual Machines offers. Any partner selling private offers on Microsoft Marketplace can use it — there is no separate seller tier to qualify for.


You enable it per offer, with the Request Private Offer toggle, on an eligible transactable offer. Because it is set at the offer level, you can open the door on the listings where a negotiated deal is likely and leave it closed on the ones where a public plan is the right path.


---


## **The work the feature creates**


The feature is the easy part. Turning inbound requests into closed deals is a workflow decision, and it has five parts worth settling before you flip the toggle:


- **Owner.** One named person or queue receives every request. A lead with no owner is a lead with no answer.
- **Routing.** The request has to reach the system your sellers work in, not a portal they check weekly. Use the referrals workspace, the APIs, or your connected CRM — whichever your team already works.
- **Response SLA.** A buyer who just asked for a price is comparing you to whoever answers first. Set a target measured in hours, and tell your team what it is.
- **Qualification.** Not every request deserves a bespoke offer. Decide what separates a request that gets a private offer from one that gets pointed at a public plan.
- **Deal-desk handoff.** Once qualified, the request becomes an offer someone has to construct, approve, and send. That handoff is where speed is usually lost.


Get those right and Request Private Offer shortens the distance from interest to offer. Skip them and it becomes a second unattended inbox.

## **Frequently asked questions**


**What is Request Private Offer on Microsoft Marketplace?** It is an offer-level setting that lets a buyer request custom pricing or terms directly from an Azure Marketplace listing page. Microsoft made it available on July 20, 2026. The request reaches the seller as a marketplace lead.


**How do buyers use it?** A buyer on an eligible listing selects the request option, optionally describes their use case, and submits. The seller receives the request as a lead and follows up by building a tailored private offer.


**Which offer types support Request Private Offer?** Eligible transactable offers: SaaS offers, Azure application offers, Azure container offers, and Azure Virtual Machines offers. It is enabled per offer with the Request Private Offer toggle.


**Where does a request go after it is submitted?** Requests flow through the commercial marketplace’s existing lead management — Marketplace referrals, supported APIs, and connected CRM integrations — and are captured as marketplace leads in the referrals workspace for your sales team.


**How is this different from sending a private offer?** Sending a private offer is seller-initiated: you build and extend it to a named buyer. Request Private Offer is buyer-initiated: the buyer asks for one from the listing, and you respond. It adds an inbound path to the same offer motion.


---


## **Takeaways**


- Request Private Offer, available since July 20, 2026, lets buyers ask for a negotiated deal from an Azure Marketplace listing — inbound demand your listing could not capture before.
- Enable it per offer with the toggle, on eligible transactable SaaS, Azure application, container, and VM offers.
- Requests arrive as marketplace leads through referrals, supported APIs, and connected CRM integrations. Route them into the system your sellers actually work.
- The feature is the easy part. Assign an owner, set a response SLA in hours, and define qualification before you turn it on.
